newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal rebels propose July peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal rebels propose July peace talks.

text.p: Tribal rebels in Bangladesh's Chittagong Hill Tracts have proposed that the next round of peace talks with the government be held on July 14, officials said on Thursday.
They said the Shanti Bahini guerrillas also offered to extend a truce in the Hill Tracts in the country's southeast to the end of September. The truce is due to expire on June 30.

The proposals were made in a letter from Ushatan Talukder, a leader of the political wing of the Shanti Bahini, sent on Wednesday to Hangsadhaja Chakma, chief of the liaison committee facilitating the talks.
"I have intimated the developments to the government," Hangsadhaja told reporters in the southern port of Chittagong on Wednesday night.
The government's response to the proposals was not immediately known.

The government and Shanti Bahini agreed on the broad outlines of a peace agreement in their last meeting in Dhaka in May, but a formal signing of the deal was delayed as the rebels sought extra time for unexplained reasons, officials said.
"Now it is expected that the deal may be signed during the proposed new round of talks," one official said.
The Shanti Bahini began an insurgency in 1973, demanding autonomy for the 5,500-square-mile (14,200-sq-km) Hill Tracts region, which borders India and Burma.
It also wants some 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers to be expelled from the region.
More than 8,500 rebels, security personnel and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee into the northeast Indian state of Tripura.

Nearly 7,000 refugees returned home in March and April following an agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi, and officials said on Thursday the next phase of repatriations was expected to begin in July.
